# Elastokines

**Elastokines**, also known as elastin-derived peptides (EDPs), are bioactive peptide fragments generated by proteolytic degradation of [[Elastin]]. Rather than being inert degradation products, elastokines function as potent signalling molecules that bind the elastin-binding protein (EBP) receptor on cell surfaces, triggering intracellular signalling cascades that amplify [[Extracellular Matrix|ECM]] degradation, promote [[Inflammation|inflammation]], and contribute to tissue ageing. The elastokine–EBP axis creates a positive feedback loop that accelerates elastic tissue destruction in ageing, COPD, atherosclerosis, and skin photoageing.

## Generation

Elastokines are produced by proteolytic cleavage of insoluble elastin by elastinolytic enzymes:

- **[[MMP-12]]:** The most potent generator of elastokines. MMP-12 cleaves insoluble elastin at specific sites, releasing bioactive fragments including the major elastokine Val-Gly-Val-Ala-Pro-Gly (VGVAPG) and other κ-elastin peptides.
- **[[MMP-2]], [[MMP-9]], [[MMP-3]]:** Contribute to elastin degradation and elastokine generation, particularly in inflammatory and ageing contexts.
- **Neutrophil elastase:** A serine protease that generates elastokines during acute inflammation.
- **Cathepsins:** Cathepsin S and L generate elastokines in the vasculature and skin.

> [!warning] Positive Feedback Loop
> Elastin degradation → elastokine generation → EBP signalling → MMP upregulation (MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-12) → further elastin degradation. This feed-forward loop is a key amplifier of age-related tissue deterioration.

## Structure & Receptor

- **Peptide fragments:** Elastokines range from 6 to ~50 kDa. The best-characterised elastokine is the hexapeptide VGVAPG (Val-Gly-Val-Ala-Pro-Gly), derived from a repeating domain of tropoelastin. Larger κ-elastin fragments (25–76 kDa) also have signalling activity.
- **EBP receptor:** Elastokines bind the elastin-binding protein (EBP), a cell-surface complex composed of:
  - **Spliced Galectin-3 (Gal-3s):** The lectin component that mediates elastokine binding
  - **Elastin-binding protein (PESN68/67 kDa):** The structural scaffold
  - **Neu-1 sialidase:** A sialidase that modulates EBP complex assembly and signalling
- **Signalling downstream of EBP:**
  - **MMP upregulation:** EBP signalling activates ERK1/2 and p38 MAPK pathways, upregulating transcription of MMP-2, MMP-9, and MMP-12
  - **Calcium influx:** Elastokines trigger intracellular Ca²⁺ release, activating calpain and downstream signalling
  - **NF-κB activation:** EBP signalling activates the NF-κB inflammatory pathway
  - **Rac1/PAK1:** Cytoskeletal remodelling and cell migration

## Physiological Roles

### Wound Healing
At low concentrations, elastokines may contribute to normal tissue remodelling by stimulating适度 MMP activity for ECM turnover and facilitating fibroblast and macrophage migration to wound sites.

### Developmental Angiogenesis
Elastokines have been implicated in developmental angiogenesis, where controlled elastin remodelling is required for vascular maturation.

## Pathological Roles

### Skin Ageing (Photoageing)
UV irradiation and [[Reactive Oxygen Species|ROS]] upregulate MMP-12 in dermal fibroblasts and macrophages, generating elastokines that:
- Amplify MMP expression (positive feedback)
- Recruit monocytes and macrophages to degraded elastic tissue
- Promote paracrine senescence in neighbouring fibroblasts
- Correlate with wrinkle formation and loss of skin elasticity

### COPD & Emphysema
Elastokines generated by MMP-12 and neutrophil elastase in the lung:
- Amplify alveolar elastin degradation
- Promote macrophage recruitment and activation
- Contribute to the protease–antiprotease imbalance driving airspace enlargement
- Serum EDPs serve as biomarkers of elastin degradation in COPD

### Atherosclerosis
Elastic lamellae fragmentation in the arterial wall generates elastokines that:
- Promote smooth muscle cell migration and proliferation
- Activate macrophages and promote foam cell formation
- Contribute to arterial stiffening and plaque instability
- Serum EDPs correlate with arterial stiffness and cardiovascular risk

### Cancer
Elastokines promote tumour-associated processes:
- Tumour angiogenesis via EBP-mediated VEGF upregulation
- Tumour cell migration and invasion through degraded elastic barriers
- Recruitment of tumour-associated macrophages

### Arterial Stiffness
Progressive elastin degradation and elastokine generation contribute to age-related arterial stiffening by:
- Reducing elastic fibre content
- Promoting collagen deposition (fibrosis)
- Activating calcification on degraded elastin surfaces

## Clinical Relevance

- **Biomarker:** Serum and urinary elastokine levels (particularly VGVAPG-containing peptides) serve as biomarkers of elastin degradation in COPD, atherosclerosis, skin ageing, and rheumatoid arthritis.
- **Therapeutic target:** Anti-elastokine strategies (blocking EBP signalling, inhibiting elastokine generation) could interrupt the positive feedback loop and slow age-related tissue deterioration.
- **COPD monitoring:** EDPs may provide a more sensitive measure of emphysema progression than pulmonary function tests alone.

## Connections

  - [[Elastin]]: Precursor substrate; elastokines are generated by proteolytic degradation of elastin
  - [[MMP-12]]: Most potent elastinolytic MMP and primary generator of elastokines
  - [[MMP-9]]: Gelatinase B that degrades elastin and generates elastokines
  - [[MMP-3]]: Stromelysin-1 contributes to elastin degradation and elastokine generation
  - [[Reactive Oxygen Species]]: ROS upregulate MMP-12, increasing elastokine generation
  - [[Inflammation]]: Elastokines are chemotactic for monocytes and macrophages, promoting inflammatory cell recruitment
  - [[Macrophages]]: Recruited by elastokines; activated macrophages produce MMP-12 that generates more elastokines
  - [[Cellular Senescence]]: Elastokines promote paracrine senescence in neighbouring fibroblasts
  - [[Angiogenesis]]: Elastokines promote tumour angiogenesis via EBP-mediated VEGF upregulation
  - [[COPD]]: Elastokines contribute to protease-antiprotease imbalance in emphysema
  - [[Arterial Stiffness]]: Elastokines contribute to arterial stiffening by promoting ECM degradation and calcification
  - [[Skin Aging]]: Elastokine-EBP axis amplifies MMP expression in photoaged skin
